title: attest: any leaf chaining to --ca is accepted as FIDO attestation
description:
git-vouch-attest:256-334 (verify) accepts any certificate that chains to --ca as a packed attestation certificate. It never checks the WebAuthn 8.2.1 packed-attestation certificate profile: X.509 v3, subject OU = "Authenticator Attestation", basicConstraints CA:FALSE. When the AAGUID extension is absent, line 325 (`cert_aaguid(...) not in (None, aaguid)`) treats that as a pass, so the AAGUID the tool prints comes only from authData, which the holder of whatever leaf key it is wrote themselves.

Failure scenario, reproduced: I built a root plus a TLS leaf (CN=www.example.com, EKU serverAuth, no OU, no AAGUID extension). I generated a software P-256 key that no device ever held, wrote it as an sk-ecdsa key, built authData with UP|AT and a chosen AAGUID, and signed authData||sha256(challenge) with the TLS key. Running `git-vouch-attest --ca root.pem soft-sk.pub soft.challenge soft.attest` exits 0 and prints "verified packed attestation, aaguid 6a1f3c2e-..., subject=CN = www.example.com". Repro script: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-mark-PROJECT-git-vouch/90586ab0-ccaf-45b4-9b85-b9df553114e9/scratchpad/a3/tls_leaf.py (args: tests/attest dir, out dir).

This is gated by which root the user passes. It becomes live when a vendor root also certifies keys whose holders can sign arbitrary data, such as PIV or OpenPGP attestation intermediates under one vendor root. My recollection is that Yubico's 2024 "Yubico Attestation Root 1" hierarchy covers FIDO, PIV and OpenPGP, but I have not verified it. If it does, then with that root a PIV slot-9a key (attestation cert chaining to the root, private key usable through PKCS#11) can "attest" a software sk key as a YubiKey. That would make this S0, because the tool would print a hardware-provenance claim that was never established. The DESIGN.md:529-533 claim "the key was created inside a device of a given model" depends on this check.

Fix: after `openssl verify` succeeds, reject the leaf unless it is v3, its subject has OU=Authenticator Attestation, and basicConstraints has CA:FALSE. These are mandatory in WebAuthn 8.2.1. Read them via `openssl x509 -noout -subject -nameopt multiline` / `-ext basicConstraints`, or with the existing take_der walker. Add fixtures from make_fixtures.py: a leaf without the OU, a CA:TRUE leaf, and a serverAuth leaf, each expected to be rejected. None of the current fixtures exercises the no-AAGUID-extension accept branch.
close_reason: git-vouch-attest check_cert_profile enforces v3, OU Authenticator Attestation, CA:FALSE, non-critical matching AAGUID ext (required always; question to Mark recorded). Tests: test_verdicts[no-ou,tls-leaf,ca-certificate,no-basic-constraints,x509-v1,x509-v2,no-aaguid-extension,aaguid-extension-critical]
